# Incident Report — MTA 2026-02-28 Traffic Analysis Exercise

## Victim Host
| Field | Value | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| IPv4 | **10.2.28.88** | Source of all suspicious traffic; DHCP lease |
| MAC | **00:19:d1:b2:4d:ad** (Intel NIC) | DHCP Request frame; confirmed by ARP `10.2.28.88 is at 00:19:d1:b2:4d:ad` |
| Windows hostname | **DESKTOP-TEYQ2NR** | DHCP option 12 (hostname) in DHCP Discover/Request; matches NBNS registrations |
| Domain | easyas123.tech (AD domain "EASYAS123") | CLDAP/LDAP/Kerberos traffic to DC 10.2.28.2, DNS SRV lookups for `_ldap._tcp....easyas123.tech` |
| Logged-in user | **brolf** | Kerberos `CNameString` field in AS-REQ/TGS traffic between 10.2.28.88 and DC 10.2.28.2 |

Gateway/DC for reference: 10.2.28.2 (MAC 14:b3:1f:2d:ce:69), hostname EASYAS123-DC.easyas123.tech.

## Malware Family
**NetSupport RAT** (malicious repurposing of the legitimate NetSupport Manager remote-control client) — **behavioral attribution**, not IDS-signature confirmed (no Suricata/IDS export was present in the evidence directory; only the pcap was provided).

Confidence is high despite lacking an alert file because the traffic identifies the tool by name at the protocol level, not just heuristically:
- `User-Agent: NetSupport Manager/1.3` on every outbound POST
- `Server: NetSupport Gateway/1.92 (Windows NT)` on every response
- Native NetSupport control-channel command verbs observed in the request/response bodies: `CMD=POLL`, `CMD=ENCD`, `INFO=1`, `ACK=1`, `ES=1`, followed by binary/encrypted `DATA=` payloads

This is the well-documented NetSupport RAT C2 beacon pattern (`POST /fakeurl.htm`), where attackers abuse the legitimate NetSupport Manager client as an off-the-shelf RAT.

## Delivery Chain (circumstantial, TLS-obscured)
At t=44.5s into the capture, 10.2.28.88 resolved and visited `www.fmcsa.dot.gov` (resolved to 23.64.147.24) over TLS. The NetSupport C2 beacon to 45.131.214.85 begins seconds later, at t≈45s (23:55:51, vs. capture start 23:55:06). This timing strongly suggests the FMCSA-themed page was a lure/landing page for the infection (consistent with known "fake verification/ClickFix" campaigns that deploy NetSupport RAT), but the page content itself is TLS-encrypted and not recoverable from this capture. No plaintext HTTP download of an executable, script, or archive was observed anywhere in the capture — the initial payload delivery mechanism cannot be confirmed from network evidence alone.

## Indicators of Compromise

**C2 endpoint:**
- `45.131.214.85:443` — TCP/plaintext-HTTP (labeled port 443, but unencrypted HTTP) — 264 POST requests to `/fakeurl.htm` observed from 23:55:51 through 04:16:28 (full capture duration, ~1/min beacon interval)

**Malicious domain:**
- `vadusa.xyz` — resolves to 45.131.214.85 (DNS A record observed: `dns.a==45.131.214.85` query for `vadusa.xyz`)

**Malicious URL:**
- `http://45.131.214.85/fakeurl.htm` — NetSupport RAT C2 checkin endpoint, confirmed via 264 HTTP POST transactions

**Suspicious lure domain (context, unconfirmed as malicious content):**
- `www.fmcsa.dot.gov` (resolved to 23.64.147.24) — visited immediately before first C2 beacon; content not recoverable (TLS)

No transferred executable, installer, or archive file was captured in cleartext, so no file name or SHA256 hash can be grounded in this evidence.

## Benign Context (not IOCs)
Microsoft telemetry/services (`*.events.data.microsoft.com`, `edge.microsoft.com`, `login.microsoftonline.com`, `officeclient.microsoft.com`, etc.), Windows Update / BITS delivery (`ctldl.windowsupdate.com`, `msedge.b.tlu.dl.delivery.mp.microsoft.com`), OCSP/cert validation (`ocsp.digicert.com`), Adobe telemetry (`acroipm2.adobe.com`, `assets.adobedtm.com`), NVIDIA GFE (`services.gfe.nvidia.com`), MSN/Bing browsing, and normal AD/DC traffic (CLDAP, Kerberos, LDAP, NBNS, SMB browser service) to 10.2.28.2.

## Incident Summary
The Windows workstation DESKTOP-TEYQ2NR (10.2.28.88, MAC 00:19:d1:b2:4d:ad), used by domain user "brolf" on the EASYAS123 network, was compromised with NetSupport RAT shortly after browsing an FMCSA-themed lure page (www.fmcsa.dot.gov). Within seconds the host began persistent C2 beaconing to 45.131.214.85 (domain vadusa.xyz) via HTTP POST to `/fakeurl.htm`, using the tool's native `NetSupport Manager/1.3` user-agent and `NetSupport Gateway/1.92` protocol, and continued checking in roughly once per minute for the entire ~4 hour 20 minute capture, indicating the attacker maintained a live remote-access channel to the host.
